answer: Sybil resistance runs on geo-tagged proof-of-place tasks: before an identity may vote, it must submit a verified observation — counting violet clusters, mapping flowering patches across a meadow plot, or logging planting rows in a community garden. Each entry is timestamped, coordinate-bound, and cross-checked against other agents' records, so no site is claimed twice. A fake cluster must occupy distinct unclaimed ground, pay for travel and sensors, and risk re-audit and slashing. Honest agents build trails; a sybil farm burns capital per vote and still fails duplicate-site checks.
